rationale: The correction of the two-gate behaviour entry registered an affected-use gap on the adverse-phase question, and it can be answered now that the pre-vote-disabled receipt exists: the use that was affected is the interpretation resting on revision 1, its comparisons and conclusion are unchanged, and the refinement the correction carries - which gate produces the separation - is carried by the sibling receipt. This submission answers that gap in a revision of the affected interpretation, citing both receipts with the compatibility reasoning they need, and updates the counterevidence item the earlier revision had to leave open.

interpretations.rationale: Final revision of this question, answering the gap the knowledge correction raised against it and folding in the refinement. The finding is unchanged: the declared prediction - that a voter already campaigning before the leader's isolation would overlap the cut-off leader's confirmation with its election - was contradicted, and the retention of this account is justified by twenty valid witnesses rather than by an absence of evidence, each trial ending its confirmations at the leader's lease (47-58ms) with no competing leader during the window. The refinement concerns only why: this run kept the isolated voter at the leader's own term, which is pre-vote holding it there, so it could not say whether the peers' known-leader refusal would suffice on its own; the sibling receipt, with pre-vote disabled, produced a live higher-term candidacy in every trial and still no overlap, which answers that question in the affirmative and is why the behaviour entry is now stated in terms of the known-leader gate rather than the combination. The counterevidence recorded here is updated accordingly: the item that said the attribution was unavailable is replaced by the point that the attribution now rests on a configuration which is legal but not the captured default, and the residual limits are the same cluster shape, the constructed history and the absence of any application read.

86f6ff19843d4db09a7d7c57c0affe41-gap-1.explanation: The affected use is this interpretation's reliance on the two-gate behaviour entry at revision 1; the correction refines the entry's attribution without changing any comparison or conclusion recorded here. This question's own receipt still carries the result - the overlap prediction came back violated and complete with all twenty adverse trials as valid witnesses, and the isolated voter stayed Candidate at the leader's own term - and the sibling receipt shows that when pre-vote is disabled the candidacy does form (terms three to five against a leader at two or three, twelve of twelve) while the separation still holds (no competing leader during any confirmation window, confirmations ending at the leader's lease in every trial). Together they attribute the separation to the peers' known-leader refusal and their heartbeat timers, with pre-vote as an additional gate that stops the candidacy from forming at all: the refinement strengthens the entry's statement and leaves this question's finding, its witnesses and its scope intact.

knowledge.assertion: The corrected entry names the known-leader refusal and the heartbeat timers as the gate that produces the separation, with pre-vote additional; this question's twenty adverse trials are the observations it rests on.

counterevidence: The attribution now rests on a configuration with pre-vote disabled, which is legal but not the captured default; the default case is this run, and the two are compared rather than conflated.
The candidacy in both runs was produced by isolating a voter rather than by catching a live campaign in a healthy cluster, so the history is constructed even where the candidacy is real.
No application read is served, so what is measured is the coexistence of a confirmation with a competing leader, not a delivered value.
The separation is a property of uniformly configured clusters; the mixed-timer findings elsewhere in this run show the configuration in which it fails.
limitations: One cluster shape (three voters plus one nonvoter, quorum two) and one set of timer values (50ms), in one process with in-memory transports.
The isolated voter was given up to three seconds to campaign; longer histories were not tried.
The negative result now spans two pre-vote configurations but still one set of timer values.
interpretations.joint_history: The second receipt belongs to the sibling question's experiment and is compatible with this account because it repeats this question's construction with one variable changed: the same hand-built four-node clusters with identical settings, the same forced transfer onto node 0, the same demotion to nonvoter, the same isolation of one voter and then of the leader with the nonvoter, and the same polling of the verification path - with PreVoteDisabled set on every node so that the higher-term candidacy this question's run could not produce does form. Its admission events are the same baseline confirmations this question relies on, and its exposure events carry the same operands, so the joined receipt refines the attribution of this question's negative result rather than replacing it.
